name: Hedgehog Agave
description: Agave stricta (hedgehog agave) is a compact, rosette-forming succulent in the Asparagaceae family, native to Mexico. It forms dense clumps of narrow, spine-tipped dark green leaves up to about 40 cm long, giving a hedgehog-like appearance. It thrives in full sun, well-draining sandy or gritty soil, and is drought-tolerant; it is suited to arid, Mediterranean, or subtropical conditions and can be used in xeric terrariums or as a potted specimen. The sap is irritating and the leaf tips are sharp—handle with care. After many years it may send up a tall flower spike; the plant is monocarpic (dies after flowering) but produces offsets for propagation.
careTips: Provide full sun or very bright light; at least 6 hours of direct sun daily
Use very well-draining, sandy or gritty soil; avoid waterlogged or heavy soils
Water sparingly; allow soil to dry thoroughly between waterings; reduce in winter
Tolerates low humidity; avoid high humidity and standing water
Protect from frost; hardy in zones 8 and above outdoors
Wear gloves when handling; sap is irritating and spines are sharp
Propagate by offsets or leaf/stem cuttings allowed to callus before planting
